description: NL->SQL questions over the `flights-2024` dataset (public/data/datasets.json): the `flights` schema and tables for all of 2024 (7,079,061 US domestic flights; flights, carriers, airports). Cases are those of evals/sql-corpus-flights.json with the dates moved to the year (the prompt's "now" is max(flight_date) = 2024-12-31; $SINCE expands on flight_date), plus month-level questions. Same scoring rules as evals/sql-corpus.json.

cases.question: number of flights per airline
reference: SELECT carrier, count(*) AS flights FROM flights GROUP BY carrier ORDER BY carrier
SELECT c.name, count(*) AS flights FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

cases.question: average departure delay by carrier
reference: SELECT carrier, avg(dep_delay) AS dep_delay FROM flights GROUP BY carrier ORDER BY carrier
SELECT c.name, avg(f.dep_delay) AS dep_delay FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

cases.question: cancellation rate per airline
reference: SELECT carrier, avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS cancellation_rate FROM flights GROUP BY carrier ORDER BY carrier
SELECT carrier, 100.0 * avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS cancellation_rate FROM flights GROUP BY carrier ORDER BY carrier
SELECT c.name, avg(f.cancelled::INTEGER) AS cancellation_rate FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name
SELECT c.name, 100.0 * avg(f.cancelled::INTEGER) AS cancellation_rate FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

reference: SELECT origin, count(*) AS departures FROM flights GROUP BY origin ORDER BY departures DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT a.name, count(*) AS departures FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON f.origin = a.code GROUP BY a.name ORDER BY departures DESC LIMIT 10
SELECT f.origin, a.name, count(*) AS departures FROM flights f JOIN airports a ON f.origin = a.code GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY departures DESC LIMIT 10

SELECT c.name, 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE arr_delay <= 15) / count(arr_delay) AS on_time_pct FROM flights JOIN carriers c ON flights.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

SELECT c.name, 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE arr_delay <= 0) / count(*) AS on_time_pct FROM flights JOIN carriers c ON flights.carrier = c.code GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY c.name

cases.note: BTS counts a flight on time when it arrives less than 15 minutes late; arriving early or on schedule is also a common reading.

cases.question: departures per hour from Atlanta on the last day
reference: SELECT date_trunc('hour', scheduled_departure) AS hour, count(*) AS departures FROM flights WHERE origin = 'ATL' AND flight_date = DATE '2024-12-31' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

cases.question: each carrier's average departure delay minus the average over all flights
reference: SELECT carrier, avg(dep_delay) - (SELECT avg(dep_delay) FROM flights) AS diff FROM flights GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT c.name AS carrier, avg(f.dep_delay) - (SELECT avg(dep_delay) FROM flights) AS diff FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
SELECT carrier, avg(dep_delay) - (SELECT avg(dep_delay) FROM flights WHERE NOT cancelled) AS diff FROM flights WHERE NOT cancelled GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

SELECT c.name AS carrier, avg(f.dep_delay) - (SELECT avg(dep_delay) FROM flights WHERE NOT cancelled) AS diff FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code WHERE NOT f.cancelled GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.note: Cancelled flights with a recorded departure delay may be included or excluded.

cases.question: median daily cancellation rate per carrier
reference: WITH d AS (SELECT f.carrier AS carrier, flight_date, avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS r FROM flights f GROUP BY ALL) SELECT carrier, median(r) AS rate FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
WITH d AS (SELECT f.carrier AS carrier, flight_date, avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS r FROM flights f GROUP BY ALL) SELECT carrier, 100 * median(r) AS rate FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH d AS (SELECT c.name AS carrier, flight_date, avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS r FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY ALL) SELECT carrier, median(r) AS rate FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

WITH d AS (SELECT c.name AS carrier, flight_date, avg(cancelled::INTEGER) AS r FROM flights f JOIN carriers c ON f.carrier = c.code GROUP BY ALL) SELECT carrier, 100 * median(r) AS rate FROM d GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
cases.note: Daily rate first, then the median per carrier; code or name, fraction or percent.

cases.question: most frequent destination for each of the 10 busiest origin airports
reference: WITH r AS (SELECT origin, dest, count(*) AS n, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY origin ORDER BY count(*) DESC) AS rn, sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY origin) AS total FROM flights GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT origin, dest, n AS flights FROM r WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10

WITH r AS (SELECT origin, dest, count(*) AS n, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY origin ORDER BY count(*) DESC) AS rn, sum(count(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY origin) AS total FROM flights GROUP BY 1, 2) SELECT origin, dest FROM r WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY total DESC LIMIT 10
cases.note: Busiest = most departures. Destination with or without its flight count.
